title: Malaysia Marathon 2026 Review: What the First Edition Was Like
seo_title: Malaysia Marathon 2026 Review | Pavilion to KLCC
meta_description: Malaysia Marathon 2026 review: 25,000 runners, a 12.30am start at Pavilion KL and a KLCC finish on 30 August, run in the middle of the haze season.
dek: Kuala Lumpur's new National Day marathon was run for the first time on 30 August 2026, from Pavilion to KLCC rather than from Dataran Merdeka. Here is what it was like, from the reporting on it.
verdict: The Malaysia Marathon arrived at full size. Its first edition, on 30 August 2026, put 25,000 runners on the streets of central Kuala Lumpur across four distances [1]. The full marathon started at 12.30am from Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, and every category finished at KLCC instead of Dataran Merdeka [1][2]. The route took in the elevated AKLEH and SUKE highways, and the city closed a long list of roads for it [1][2]. It was also run during the haze, which had disrupted training in the weeks before [2]. If you want a big, World Athletics-recognised city marathon in KL with a night start, it is a serious new option. Watch the air quality in the final week.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition in Numbers
paragraphs: The first Malaysia Marathon was run in the early hours of Sunday 30 August 2026, as part of the 69th National Day celebrations, and drew 25,000 local and international runners [1]. Bernama reported 2,000 in the full marathon, 8,000 in the half marathon, 5,000 in the 10 km and 10,000 in the 5 km fun run [1].
Tourism Minister Tiong King Sing flagged off the full marathon near Pavilion Kuala Lumpur [1]. The event has World Athletics recognition [1].

sections.heading: A Midnight Start, and a New Finish
paragraphs: The start times are the first thing to plan around: the full marathon at 12.30am, the half marathon at 2am, the 10 km at 3.30am and the fun run at 7.30am [1][2]. Every distance except the fun run started at Pavilion, and all finished at KLCC [2]. Most Kuala Lumpur road races use Dataran Merdeka for both [2].

The full-marathon route ran along Jalan Bukit Bintang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan, through the old city on Jalan Tun HS Lee and Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, then out onto the AKLEH and SUKE elevated highways and back via Jalan Ampang and Jalan P Ramlee to KLCC [2]. Bernama said the full marathon included a 900-metre climb on the AKLEH [1]. The highway sections are likely to be the hardest part of the course.

sections.heading: Road Closures and the Haze
paragraphs: Roads across the city centre were closed in phases from Friday night until Sunday afternoon, including stretches of Jalan Ampang, Jalan P Ramlee and Jalan Bukit Bintang in front of Pavilion [2]. Race pack collection was at the Premiera Hotel on 28 and 29 August [2].

The race was run during the regional haze episode. Paultan.org noted before the race that training would have been disrupted by it [2]. The race went ahead. A week later, the PJ Half Marathon was cancelled at the last minute because of the same haze [3].

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you want a large Kuala Lumpur marathon on a route that shows off the city centre, yes. Twenty-five thousand runners in year one, World Athletics recognition and a new Pavilion-to-KLCC route make it a real alternative to the city's established races.

Plan the night. A 12.30am start means racing through the night, not at dawn, so plan how you will get to the start and rest beforehand. And because this is a late-August race in a haze-prone season, keep your travel plans flexible.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2026 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Malaysia Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: 25,000 runners took part in the first edition on 30 August 2026: 2,000 in the full marathon, 8,000 in the half marathon, 5,000 in the 10 km and 10,000 in the 5 km fun run, according to Bernama. It was held as part of Malaysia's 69th National Day celebrations.

faqs.question: What time does the Malaysia Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2026 the full marathon started at 12.30am, the half marathon at 2am, the 10 km at 3.30am and the 5 km fun run at 7.30am. The longer races started near Pavilion Kuala Lumpur and all distances finished at KLCC.

faqs.question: What is the Malaysia Marathon route like?
faqs.answer: A city-centre course that also uses the elevated highways. In 2026 it ran from Pavilion along Bukit Bintang, Sultan Ismail and Raja Chulan, through the old city, then out on the AKLEH and SUKE highways and back via Jalan Ampang to KLCC. Bernama reported a 900-metre climb on the AKLEH.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the first edition, run on 30 August 2026. Replaces a pre-race preview. Bernama's field-by-distance figures are published on race day and may be entry numbers, not finishers. The '900-metre climb' is Bernama's phrase and is attributed to it. No rating.
